headline: Treasury doubled its long-end buybacks and the 30y fell 10bp — then the $16bn 20y still left dealers with 12.5%.
stance: Bessent doubled the size cap on long-end liquidity buybacks to at least $4bn, and the long end got its first real relief in a week. The 20y then cleared at 5.204% with 12.5% left on dealer books, more than last week's 30y took: the bid was rescued, not repaired.

news.head: Treasury doubles long-end buybacks
news.body: Caps in the 10y–20y and 20y–30y buckets rise from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation, running Sept 9 through Nov 4. Nothing is bought before then.

news.head: $16bn 20y auction: dealers left with 12.5%
news.body: High yield 5.204%, bid-to-cover 2.53, indirects 62.9%. Dealers took 12.5% against 11.5% on last week's 30y — the announcement moved price, not demand.

news.head: July minutes: the hike case ran wider than three votes
news.body: Behind the 9-3 hold, many participants said tightening would be needed if inflation did not fall. Written before the July payroll contraction.

implications: Treasury is managing the long end directly rather than waiting for demand. Read it as support for duration and as a tell about how much strain officials were seeing.
The Iran escalation is inflationary before it is geopolitical. Crude bid with Hormuz shut feeds the exact path that left many on the committee open to a hike.

watch.head: Walmart before the bell
watch.body: Target comps ran +3.8% and Lowe's +0.2% — essentials against discretionary. Walmart decides which of those is the economy and which is company-specific.

watch.head: Jobless claims and Philly Fed, 8:30am ET
watch.body: The first labour read since July payrolls contracted. The minutes predate that print, so claims carry more than usual into Jackson Hole next week.

watch.head: Whether the buyback bid survives without a headline
watch.body: Wednesday's move came off an announcement. The operations do not begin until Sept 9, so the next three weeks are sentiment rather than actual flow.

watch.head: Crude into a sanctions escalation
watch.body: Brent near $92 and WTI $84.51 this morning, up more than 5% across four sessions. Hormuz is the physical constraint; enforcement risk now sits on top.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 30y 5.187%, -10bp; 10y 4.65%, -6bp — the whole move came off the buyback headline, before a single bond has actually been repurchased.
The $16bn 20y cleared at 5.204%, bid-to-cover 2.53, dealers left with 12.5% against 11.5% on last week's 30y. Price improved; the buyer base did not.
Gold $4,492/oz, -0.6% (~6am ET), holding most of a 4%-plus Wednesday jump. Lower real yields did that, not fear — and spec length is already 91st %ile.
sections.positioning: New this week: spec net long 5y Treasuries jumped 11 points to the 93rd %ile, with the 2y standing at the 98th. The front end is positioned long into minutes that show a live hike constituency.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Target comps +3.8% with full-year sales growth guided up to about 5%; Lowe's comps +0.2% and guidance cut to the low end. Essentials working, home improvement not.
Futures firm this morning — S&P +0.16%, Nasdaq 100 +0.42% at 1:45am ET — into Walmart, Alibaba, Deere and Ross Stores all reporting today.
sections.positioning: The new equity extreme is in vol, not the index: spec net short VIX futures fell 12 points to the 10th %ile this week, hedgers at the opposite end. That short went on before the escalation.

single_name.note: German American Bancorp — new to the screen today, insider buy filed Aug 18, trading above its 200-day. 6.4 days to cover at a 0.41% borrow: no short base to squeeze.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: The backstop covers government paper only. Corporate spreads widened in the same week the people who make the market cut what they are willing to hold.
Note whose balance sheet this is: Treasury refinancing its own debt, not the Fed adding reserves. Bank reserves $2,944bn and a balance sheet +1.75% y/y are untouched by it.
sections.positioning: The new credit extreme: dealer net high-yield inventory fell 29 points to the 5th %ile of three years, IG at the 14th as background. Thin inventory is cheap until somebody needs to sell into it.
